---
title: Databases
icon: Database
description: Create databases, define typed tables, write rows, and query them with a fluent builder, all backed by real PostgreSQL with permissions enforced in the database.
---

import { ShieldCheck, KeyRound, Radio, FolderClosed } from 'lucide-react';

An Applad database is real PostgreSQL. You define **tables** with typed
**columns**, write **rows**, and read them back through a fluent query builder or
the REST API. Access is governed by [permissions](/build/permissions) that Applad
enforces with PostgreSQL row-level security, so a rule you set is a rule the
database keeps, not one your client is trusted to honour.

The shape is: a **database** holds **tables**, a table has **columns** and
**rows**. You define the schema once (from the console, a migration, or a setup
script), then your app reads and writes rows.

<Callout title="Two kinds of caller">
  Defining databases, tables, columns and indexes is an operator task. Do it with
  a **server API key** (`x-applad-key`) from a trusted environment, not from
  end-user code. Reading and writing rows is what your app does at runtime, with
  the signed-in user's **session** (`Authorization: Bearer <secret>`). Both hit
  the same `/v1/databases` routes.
</Callout>

## The client

Client examples below use a project-scoped SDK client. See
[authentication](/build/authentication) for how a user signs in and how the session
token is attached.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
import { Applad } from '@mittolabs/applad';

const client = new Applad({ endpoint: 'https://api.applad.io', projectId: '<projectId>' });
const db = client.databases;
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
final client = Applad(endpoint: 'https://api.applad.io', projectId: '<projectId>');
final db = client.databases;
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Build a database

Defining the schema and writing the first rows follows one path: create a
database, add a table, give it typed columns, refine it with indexes and
relationships, then write rows.

<Steps>

<Step>

### Databases

A database is a namespace for tables. Create one, and pass its id to everything
below.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const database = await db.createDatabase('app', 'app');
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
final database = await db.createDatabase(name: 'app', databaseId: 'app');
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

`databaseId` is optional. Omit it and Applad generates one (the SDKs send
`unique()`). The full set of database operations:

| SDK (Dart) | SDK (JS) | Route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createDatabase(name:, databaseId:)` | `createDatabase(name, databaseId?)` | `POST /v1/databases` |
| `listDatabases()` | `listDatabases()` | `GET /v1/databases` |
| `getDatabase(id)` | `getDatabase(id)` | `GET /v1/databases/{id}` |
| `updateDatabase(id, name)` | `updateDatabase(id, name)` | `PUT /v1/databases/{id}` |
| `deleteDatabase(id)` | `deleteDatabase(id)` | `DELETE /v1/databases/{id}` |

`listDatabases()` returns `{ "total": <n>, "databases": [...] }`.

</Step>

<Step>

### Tables

A table is a typed collection of rows. Create it with the permissions that decide
who may read and write it:

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await db.createTable('app', 'messages', {
  tableId: 'messages',
  permissions: ['read("users")', 'create("users")'],
  documentSecurity: true,
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
await db.createTable(
  databaseId: 'app',
  name: 'messages',
  tableId: 'messages',
  permissions: ['read("users")', 'create("users")'], // any signed-in user
  documentSecurity: true,   // each row may also carry its own permissions
);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

`permissions` are `action("role")` strings applied to every row in the table.
`documentSecurity` turns on per-row permissions in addition to the table ones.
Both are covered under [Permissions](#permissions) below and in full on the
[permissions](/build/permissions) page. Omit `tableId` to have one generated.

| Operation | Route |
| --- | --- |
| Create table | `POST /v1/databases/{databaseId}/tables` |
| List tables | `GET /v1/databases/{databaseId}/tables` |
| Get table | `GET /v1/databases/{databaseId}/tables/{tableId}` |
| Update table (`name`, `permissions`, `enabled`) | `PUT /v1/databases/{databaseId}/tables/{tableId}` |
| Delete table | `DELETE /v1/databases/{databaseId}/tables/{tableId}` |

</Step>

<Step>

### Columns

Columns are typed and added one at a time, each with its own type-specific
options. Every column type accepts `required` (reject rows that omit it),
`array` (store a list of that type), and `default`.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await db.createStringColumn('app', 'messages', 'body', { required: true, size: 8000 });
await db.createIntegerColumn('app', 'messages', 'priority', { min: 0, max: 5, defaultValue: 0 });
await db.createBooleanColumn('app', 'messages', 'pinned', { defaultValue: false });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
// A required string, capped at 8000 characters.
await db.createStringColumn(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages',
  key: 'body', required_: true, size: 8000,
);

// An integer with a range.
await db.createIntegerColumn(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages',
  key: 'priority', min: 0, max: 5, defaultValue: 0,
);

// A boolean with a default.
await db.createBooleanColumn(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages',
  key: 'pinned', defaultValue: false,
);

// An enum constrained to a fixed set.
await db.createEnumColumn(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages',
  key: 'status', elements: ['sent', 'delivered', 'read'], required_: true,
);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Type-specific options:

| Type | Route suffix | Options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| String | `/columns/string` | `size` |
| Integer | `/columns/integer` | `min`, `max` |
| Float | `/columns/float` | `min`, `max` |
| Boolean | `/columns/boolean` | None |
| Enum | `/columns/enum` | `elements` (required) |
| Email | `/columns/email` | None |
| URL | `/columns/url` | None |
| Datetime | `/columns/datetime` | None |

<Callout title="Not every type has a typed SDK helper">
  The Dart client ships helpers for string, integer, boolean and enum columns;
  the JS client ships string, integer and boolean. The other types (float, email,
  url, datetime, and enum from JS) are created by calling the route directly, for
  example `POST /v1/databases/{databaseId}/tables/{tableId}/columns/email` with a
  JSON body `{ "key": "contact", "required": true }`.
</Callout>

List and delete columns:

```dart
await db.listColumns('app', 'messages');
await db.deleteColumn('app', 'messages', 'priority');
```

`listColumns` returns `{ "total": <n>, "columns": [...] }`.

</Step>

<Step>

### Indexes

Add an index to speed up filters and ordering on a column. Give it a key, a type
(`key`, `unique`, or `fulltext`), and the columns it covers:

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await db.createIndex('app', 'messages', 'by_created', 'key', ['created_at'], ['DESC']);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
await db.createIndex(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages',
  key: 'by_created', type: 'key',
  columns: ['created_at'], orders: ['DESC'],
);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

`orders` is optional and pairs positionally with `columns`. List with
`listIndexes('app', 'messages')`, remove with `deleteIndex('app', 'messages', 'by_created')`.

</Step>

<Step>

### Relationships

A relationship is a typed link between two tables. Create it as a column on the
source table, naming the related table and the relationship type:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/databases/app/tables/messages/columns/relationship \
  -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "relatedTableId": "users",
    "type": "manyToOne",
    "key": "author",
    "twoWay": false,
    "onDelete": "setNull"
  }'
```

`type` is one of `oneToOne`, `oneToMany`, `manyToOne`, `manyToMany` (defaults to
`oneToMany`). `twoWay` and `twoWayKey` create the reverse link on the related
table; `onDelete` controls what happens to a row when its related row is removed.
List with `GET /v1/databases/{databaseId}/tables/{tableId}/relationships` and
delete with `DELETE .../relationships/{relationshipId}`.

<Callout title="Related-column selection is not wired up yet">
  You can define relationships and they exist as real foreign keys, but expanding
  a related column inside a row query (the `select('author(name)')` form) is not
  applied by the server today. Fetch the related row by its id in a second call.
</Callout>

</Step>

<Step>

### Rows

A row is one record. Create, read, update and delete them at runtime with the
signed-in user's session.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const row = await db.createRow('app', 'messages', { body: 'hello', status: 'sent' }, {
  permissions: ['read("users")'],
});
const rowId = row['$id'];

await db.getRow('app', 'messages', rowId);
await db.listRows('app', 'messages', { limit: 25, offset: 0 });
await db.updateRow('app', 'messages', rowId, { data: { status: 'read' } });
await db.deleteRow('app', 'messages', rowId);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
// Create
final row = await db.createRow(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages',
  data: {'body': 'hello', 'status': 'sent'},
  permissions: ['read("users")'],
);
final rowId = row['\$id'];

// Read one
final one = await db.getRow(databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages', rowId: rowId);

// List (offset pagination)
final page = await db.listRows(databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages', limit: 25, offset: 0);

// Update (partial, send only the fields that change)
await db.updateRow(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages', rowId: rowId,
  data: {'status': 'read'},
);

// Delete
await db.deleteRow(databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages', rowId: rowId);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

`rowId` is optional on create; omit it for a generated id. `updateRow` is a
`PATCH` and merges: fields you leave out keep their current value. `listRows`
returns `{ "total": <n>, "rows": [...] }`.

</Step>

</Steps>

### System fields on a row

Every row carries system fields alongside your own columns. Your columns sit at
the **top level** of the row object, merged with these:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `$id` | The row's id |
| `$tableId` | The table it belongs to |
| `$databaseId` | The database it belongs to |
| `$createdAt` | When it was created (RFC 3339) |
| `$updatedAt` | When it was last updated |
| `$permissions` | The row's own permission strings (present when document security is on) |

```json
{
  "$id": "a1b2c3",
  "$tableId": "messages",
  "$databaseId": "app",
  "$createdAt": "2026-01-04T10:00:00Z",
  "$updatedAt": "2026-01-04T10:00:00Z",
  "$permissions": ["read(\"users\")"],
  "body": "hello",
  "status": "sent"
}
```

```dart
print(row['\$id']);      // system field
print(row['body']);     // your column, top-level
```

## Querying

`from(databaseId, tableId)` starts a query. Filters, ordering and pagination
chain onto it, and `get()` runs it:

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Dart']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const result = await db
  .from('app', 'messages')
  .equal('status', 'sent')
  .greaterThan('priority', 0)
  .orderDesc('created_at')
  .limit(50)
  .get();

console.log(result.total);
for (const row of result.rows) console.log(row['body']);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Dart">
```dart
final result = await db
    .from('app', 'messages')
    .equal('status', 'sent')
    .greaterThan('priority', 0)
    .orderDesc('created_at')
    .limit(50)
    .get();

print(result.total);          // total matching rows (before limit/offset)
for (final row in result.rows) {
  print(row['body']);
}
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Chained filters combine with **AND**. The builder returns `{ total, rows }`.

### Operators

Each of these is a method on the builder. `field` is a column name; string
matches (`contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`) are case-insensitive.

| Method | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `equal(field, value)` | `field` equals `value` |
| `notEqual(field, value)` | `field` does not equal `value` |
| `lessThan(field, value)` | `field` is less than `value` |
| `lessThanOrEqual(field, value)` | `field` is less than or equal to `value` |
| `greaterThan(field, value)` | `field` is greater than `value` |
| `greaterThanOrEqual(field, value)` | `field` is greater than or equal to `value` |
| `contains(field, value)` | `field` contains the substring `value` |
| `startsWith(field, value)` | `field` starts with `value` |
| `endsWith(field, value)` | `field` ends with `value` |
| `search(field, value)` | full-text search on `field` (PostgreSQL `tsvector`) |
| `isNull(field)` | `field` is `NULL` |
| `isNotNull(field)` | `field` is not `NULL` |

```dart
// Everything unread that mentions "deploy", newest first.
final hits = await db
    .from('app', 'messages')
    .notEqual('status', 'read')
    .search('body', 'deploy')
    .orderDesc('created_at')
    .get();
```

### Ordering and pagination

`orderAsc(field)` / `orderDesc(field)` sort the result; without one, rows come
back newest-first (`created_at` descending). `limit(n)` caps the page (default
25) and `offset(n)` skips rows:

```dart
// Page 2 of 25.
final page2 = await db
    .from('app', 'messages')
    .orderDesc('created_at')
    .limit(25)
    .offset(25)
    .get();
```

<Callout title="Supported today vs. present but not applied">
  Offset pagination (`limit` + `offset`), the operators in the table above, and
  `orderAsc`/`orderDesc` all run server-side. The builder also exposes
  `between(...)`, `cursorAfter(...)` and `select(...)`, but the server does not
  apply these yet, so a query that relies on one of them will not filter,
  paginate or project the way its name suggests. Stick to `offset` for paging and
  fetch the columns you need from the full row until these are wired up.
</Callout>

## Permissions

Access to every table and row is governed by [permissions](/build/permissions), which
Applad enforces with PostgreSQL row-level security. Because the rule lives in the
database, it holds for the query builder, the REST API and the realtime read path
alike. The [permissions](/build/permissions) page is the full reference; the essentials
for databases:

A permission is an `action("role")` string. Actions are `read`, `create`,
`update` and `delete`. Roles are resolved **server-side from the caller's own
identity and team memberships** on every request. A client never sends its own
roles.

| Role | Matches |
| --- | --- |
| `any` | everyone, signed in or not |
| `users` | any signed-in user |
| `user:<id>` | one specific user |
| `team:<id>` | every member of a team |
| `team:<id>/<role>` | members of a team who hold a role |

### Table permissions vs. document security

A permission set on the **table** applies to every row in it, which is right for
"any signed-in user may read this table". Turn on **document security**
(`documentSecurity: true` when you create the table) and each row *also* carries
its own `$permissions`: access is granted when the table grants it **or** the row
grants it. That is what lets one shared table hold data that different groups see
different slices of.

```dart
// Readable by the channel's team, editable and deletable only by its author.
await db.createRow(
  databaseId: 'app', tableId: 'messages',
  data: {'channel_id': channelId, 'body': 'hello'},
  permissions: [
    'read("team:$channelId")',
    'update("user:$myUserId")',
    'delete("user:$myUserId")',
  ],
);
```

With that in place a member of the channel's team sees the message, a non-member
sees nothing, and only the author can change or remove it.

<Callout title="Fails closed">
  A row that does not grant a caller `read` is simply invisible to them. List
  queries skip it rather than erroring. If you build a document-security table and
  see no rows, check that each row grants `read` to a role the caller actually
  holds.
</Callout>

### Owner column

If a table has an owner column (a column named `owner_id` or `user_id` holding
the id of the user who owns each row), that user always has full access to their
own rows, without you setting per-row permissions for them.

## Errors

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | Missing required field on a create call, or an invalid request body |
| `403` | The caller lacks permission to create, read, update or delete (code `permission_denied`) |
| `404` | The database, table, column or row does not exist |

A row that fails a column's validation rule (a required field left out, an enum
value outside `elements`, a number outside `min`/`max`) returns a validation
error naming the offending field.
